facts.text: ISO 15998 was the former functional-safety standard for electronic machine-control systems on earth-moving machinery; ISO 13766 is the electromagnetic compatibility standard for earth-moving machinery.
facts.quote: ISO 15998 was the former functional-safety standard for electronic machine-control systems on earth-moving machinery, withdrawn in 2022 and replaced by ISO 19014, and ISO 13766 is the standard for electromagnetic compatibility of such machines.

facts.text: ISO 15998:2008, titled “Machine-control systems using electronic components, performance criteria and tests for functional safety,” and its companion ISO/TS 15998-2:2012 were withdrawn on 14 June 2022 and replaced by the ISO 19014 series.
facts.quote: ISO 15998:2008 ("Machine-control systems using electronic components, performance criteria and tests for functional safety") and its companion ISO/TS 15998-2:2012 were withdrawn on 14 June 2022 and replaced by the ISO 19014 series

facts.text: ISO 16001:2017 refers to ISO 15998 for environmental conditions and states that ISO 19014-3 can be used as an alternative.
facts.quote: ISO 16001:2017 points to ISO 15998 for environmental conditions and notes that "ISO 19014-3 can be used as an alternative"

facts.text: A reader encountering ISO 15998 in a supplier document should treat the reference as dated and ask for the ISO 19014 equivalent.
facts.quote: A reader who sees ISO 15998 in a supplier document should treat it as dated and ask for the ISO 19014 equivalent.

facts.text: Under ISO 13766 electromagnetic compatibility requirements for earth-moving machinery, electronics must neither emit radio interference that disturbs other equipment nor be disturbed by external interference.
facts.quote: ISO 13766 covers electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) for earth-moving machinery: the electronics must neither emit radio interference that disturbs other equipment nor be disturbed by interference from outside.

facts.text: ISO 16001 requires an object detection system to meet ISO 13766 electromagnetic compatibility requirements.
facts.quote: ISO 16001 requires an object detection system to meet it

facts.text: The South African mining industry's MOSH laboratory phase includes electromagnetic compatibility testing among its TRL4 bench tests.
facts.quote: the South African mining industry's MOSH laboratory phase lists EMC testing among its TRL4 bench tests

facts.text: Withdrawn standards pose a risk in a fast project because an old data sheet may still cite the withdrawn ISO 15998 standard.
facts.quote: Withdrawn standards are a trap in a fast project: an old data sheet may cite ISO 15998, which no longer exists

facts.text: Electromagnetic compatibility matters for automatic braking because a brake request travels on an electronic network and radar shares the air with other radios.
facts.quote: EMC matters because a brake request travels on an electronic network and a radar shares the air with other radios

facts.text: In an on-road case, radio-frequency coexistence was one reason a factory emergency brake was disabled.
facts.quote: the booklet notes radio-frequency coexistence as one reason a factory emergency brake was disabled in an on-road case
